meta.subtitle: Two worlds in one process are still two machines — and IsHost is false for both of them here

views.label: One enum builds the topology

views.label: A world is its flags
views.note: GameServer, GameClient, GameThinClient. Every netcode question is a bit test on these.

views.label: The AND that is false here
views.note: IsHost is IsClient AND IsServer on one world. Separate worlds can never satisfy it.

views.label: They talk over a socket anyway
views.note: Same process, same port. IPC for the in-process pair, real UDP for everyone else.

boundaries.label: one process · separate worlds · separate entity managers · separate singletons

cards.title: A world is a flag word, and nothing more
items: IsServer is a bit test for GameServer
IsClient is a bit test for GameClient, or thin client
IsThinClient is a bit test for GameThinClient
IsHost is IsClient and IsServer on the same world, which is an AND, not an opinion

cards.title: Why IsHost is false in this project
items: The bootstrap builds ServerWorld and ClientWorld as two separate worlds
Each carries exactly one of the two flags, so the AND cannot hold
One world carrying both flags exists only behind an experimental define
So code that branches on host behaviour takes the two-world path here, always

cards.title: The thin client is an amputation, not a setting
items: It is built from the thin client simulation filter only
No presentation, no rendering, no interpolated ghost application
It exists to hold a connection open and generate command traffic
Anything gated on the client filter simply is not there, which is usually the surprise

cards.title: Read it live, in one line
items: Loop World.All and print the name next to the flags
One ServerWorld across every editor instance, or roles are not applied
A client with no NetworkId stopped before admission
A client with a NetworkId but no in-game flag stopped before the snapshot stream
